correctness.rationale: For each plant the exact fixed-m deletion probability is a_m=C(v−d,s)/C(v,s); for two plants with intersection t, joint probability b_m(t)=C(v−2d+t,s)/C(v,s). Summing covariances gives exact Var(X_m) at any stage. Regularity ensures ∑_{i<j}|N_i∩N_j|=v C(d,2)=C(v,2) so intersection mean is one. Pascal finite differences yield Δ² b_m(t)=C(v−2d+t,s−2)/C(v,s)≥0; the support line through t=0,1 proves universal variance lower bound. In the window 2d−2≤m≤v−2 the first second difference is strictly positive, so any intersection t≥2 raises variance by at least 2Δ²; mean one forces such t unless all intersections are exactly one. The latter square symmetric 2-(v,d,1) incidence design is precisely a projective plane; finite fields give existence for every prime-power q. Double-loss cutoff follows union size 2d−t. Independently enumerated all deletion subsets for Fano and q=3 planes and a degree-preserving switch at every m, including Fano variances 4/25 and 48/175. This is bounded corroboration, not proof for all q.

value.rationale: Mean secondary-extinction robustness is identical for all d-regular networks with the same v, so exact minimization of stagewise variance is a distinct risk measure with a natural ecological interpretation. Identifying all extremizers simultaneously as projective-plane designs and the sharp first double-extinction threshold with an explicit strict gap gives a mathematically motivated extremal result bridging incidence design theory and network reliability. It does not model heterogeneous or dynamical ecological networks.

limitations: The result is proved for projective-plane parameter biregular graphs and fixed-count uniform deletions only; finite field tests p=2,3 cannot establish all prime-power cases.
